title: Light Building
subtitle: Museum pavilion of translucent beer crates, Atelier Kempe Thill, Rotterdam 2001 / construction

steps.title: 1 Foundation
steps.text: Timber sleepers spread the load on the gravel; driven steel anchors hold the rusty steel channel that takes the first course.

steps.title: 2 Floor joists
steps.text: Timber joists every 50 cm span across the steel channel; the plank floor is laid on them.

steps.title: 3 Floor and first courses
steps.text: On the plank floor, standard Dutch beer crates (395 × 295 × 235 mm), a colourless translucent edition, are stacked in stack bond on the channel: long walls 37 crates, end walls 11.

steps.title: 4 Tie rods
steps.text: Every second course a pair of threaded rods with clamp plates; vertical rods every second crate post-tension the crate wall. Steel frames line the door openings through the full wall depth.

steps.title: 5 Walls
steps.text: 25 courses, about 2,270 crates, give a 6 m high load-bearing translucent wall.

steps.title: 6 Doors and roof
steps.text: Rusty steel double doors on all four sides; a galvanised trapezoidal deck in a steel edge closes the box. Built by six people in one day.

steps.title: Exploded axonometric
steps.text: Like a building-block manual: at the front corner the top courses come apart crate by crate, so the stack bond and the tie rods through the crates show. The roof lifts off, the steel channel, sleepers and anchors drop. Every crate is its own object.

steps.title: Exploded axonometric with floor
steps.text: The same, with the wall raised to show the plank floor on its joists.
